FARMERS’ MARKET NUTRITION PROGRAM WPPM #800-30 Subject: Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program Item: Nutrition Education Documentation

Revised January 27, 2023 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 2

PURPOSE: To establish procedures for offering nutrition education and meeting documentation requirements for the Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP). POLICY: I. Local agency (LA) staff must: A. Provide nutrition education that emphasizes the use and nutritional value of fruits and vegetables seasonally available at WIC-authorized farmers’ markets to all family representatives/caretakers who receive FMNP benefits. B. Offer FMNP nutrition education that is culturally appropriate and meets the nutrition education requirements as specified in the WPPM 400 series. C. Document FMNP nutrition education contacts (NEC) on NE Documentation screen in the WIC Web Information System Exchange (WIC WISE). PROCEDURES: I. A competent professional authority (CPA) must provide a fruits and vegetables-related NEC to the FMNP benefit recipient. Refer to WPPM 130-00. A. Nutrition education must emphasize the relationship between proper nutrition and the overall concept of good health, including the importance of consuming fresh fruits and vegetables. Educational topics can include, but are not limited to: 1. Health benefits of fruits and vegetables. 2. Increasing the intake of fruits and vegetables. 3. Cooking with fruits and vegetables. 4. Types of fruits and vegetables grown in California. 5. Selection, storage, preparation and preservation of California-grown fruits and vegetables. 6. Health benefits associated with the physical activity of visiting farmers’ markets and home gardening. B. The FMNP NEC satisfies the WIC requirements for a secondary NEC. II. LA staff must document the fruits and vegetables-related nutrition education topic(s) discussed and the type of contact provided in WIC WISE for the FMNP benefit recipient. LA staff have the discretion to document for all eligible family members. A. When FMNP nutrition education is provided at the time of certification/ recertification or an individual follow-up nutrition contact, both the

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 2 of 2 January 27, 2023 certification/recertification or nutrition counseling and the FMNP NEC must be documented, using the state-developed topic, in WIC WISE. FARMERS’ MARKET NUTRITION PROGRAM WPPM #800-41 Subject: FMNP Benefit Management Item: FMNP Benefit Accountability and Integrity

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 2 February 10, 2026 PURPOSE: To ensure accountability and maintain the integrity of the Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) benefits when provided to local agencies (LAs) for distribution. POLICY: I. LAs are responsible for the security, integrity, and accountability of FMNP benefits. LAs must: A. Allocate FMNP benefits appropriately to their sites. B. Issue FMNP benefits to eligible families. C. Use CDPH/WIC developed queries and reports to monitor FMNP benefit inventory, management and oversight to ensure maximum issuance. PROCEDURES: I. Allocating, issuing, and transferring FMNP benefits. A. Allocating FMNP benefits to LA sites. 1. Authorized LA staff must allocate the FMNP benefits to sites in WIC WISE Admin module. 2. Follow the procedures in Allocating FMNP Benefits job aid. 3. Cooperate with CDPH/WIC in mid-season with benefit inventory status updates to best manage/redistribute available benefits statewide. B. Issuing FMNP benefits to families. 1. Provide and document the completion of FMNP Benefit Use and Nutrition Education contact prior to issuing FMNP benefits. Refer to WPPM 800-20, WPPM 800-30, and the Documenting FMNP Education job aid. 2. Issue FMNP benefits to families from the individual site. LA staff must log into the individual site where the benefits are assigned to issue benefits. Refer to Issuing and Voiding FMNP Benefits job aid. C. Transferring FMNP benefits from one site to another site. 1. LA staff can transfer unissued FMNP benefits from one site to another within the same LA on the Site Allocation screen by: a. Increasing or decreasing the number of families allocated to each site. D. Transferring FMNP benefits from one LA to another LA. 1. Transferring of FMNP benefits from one LA to another is a state level function in WIC WISE. LAs must request and receive written approval from the

FARMERS’ MARKET NUTRITION PROGRAM WPPM #800-41 Subject: FMNP Benefit Management Item: FMNP Benefit Accountability and Integrity

Revised February 10, 2026 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 2 of 2

CDPH/WIC Farmers’ Market Coordinator to transfer surplus or unused FMNP benefits from one LA to another. II. End of season reconciliation procedures will be completed by CDPH/WIC. A. WIC Web Information System Exchange (WIC WISE) will automatically remove unissued benefits at the end of the season. AUTHORITY: 7 CFR §248.4(a)(11) 7 CFR §248.10(f)(2) and (3) CROSS REFERENCE: WPPM 800-20 Instruction on using FMNP Benefits WPPM 800-30 Nutrition Education Documentation RESOURCES: Allocating FMNP Benefits on the Local Agency SharePoint Site (LASS) Documenting FMNP Education (LASS) Issuing and Voiding FMNP Benefits (LASS)

FARMERS’ MARKET NUTRITION PROGRAM WPPM #800-43 Subject: FMNP Benefits Management Guidelines Item: Issuance of FMNP Benefits

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 2 July 18, 2025 PURPOSE: To establish procedures for benefits issuance protocol for the Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) provided by the California Department of Public Health/Women, Infants and Children Division (CDPH/WIC). POLICY: I. Local agencies (LAs) must establish a written FMNP benefits issuance protocol to ensure staff issue FMNP benefits to all WIC families in a consistent, fair, and equitable manner. PROCEDURES: I. When developing the procedure for issuing FMNP benefits, LA staff must: A. Offer only one FMNP benefit per household per season with at least one family member who is a current WIC participant in one of the following categories: 1. Pregnant. 2. Breastfeeding. 3. Non-breastfeeding. 4. Infant after the six-month birthday. 5. Child. B. Retain the LA FMNP benefits issuance policy and procedures for review and audit for three years following the final payment of the contract. C. Train all LA staff on the issuance policy, including the need to apply the procedures in a consistent, fair, and equitable manner. D. Ensure no conflict of interest exists between LA staff and participating farmers/farmers’ markets. E. Comply with civil rights requirements during FMNP benefits issuance and activities. II. FMNP benefits must be issued through and documented in the WIC Web Information System Exchange (WIC WISE). III. LA staff must not issue FMNP benefits to themselves, their relatives, or close friends. Refer to WPPM 140-10. IV. The LA must assess agency-wide FMNP benefit usage at the end of each July to determine the likelihood of using all FMNP benefits assigned to that LA during that

FARMERS’ MARKET NUTRITION PROGRAM WPPM #800-43 Subject: FMNP Benefits Management Guidelines Item: Issuance of FMNP Benefits

Revised July 18, 2025 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 2 of 2 season in order to maximize the number of FMNP benefits issued to participants statewide. A. LAs must report these findings to CDPH/WIC by August 1 of each season. V. The LA must issue all FMNP benefits by September 30 of each season. AUTHORITY: 7 CFR §248.7 7 CFR §248.10(a)(7) CROSS REFERENCE: WPPM 140-10 WIC Services for Employees and Relatives WPPM 230-10 Priority Ranking System WPPM 800-41 FMNP Benefits Accountability and Integrity

Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program WPPM #800-50 Subject: FMNP Program Complaints Item: FMNP Program Complaints

Revised July 18, 2025 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 1 PURPOSE: To establish procedures for the complaint process for the Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP). POLICY: I. Local agency (LA) staff must inform family representatives/caretakers how to report complaints related to FMNP. II. LA staff must document and report complaints received regarding the FMNP to California Department of Public Health/Women, Infants and Children (CDPH/WIC) using the FMNP Complaint Form. PROCEDURES: I. LA staff must: A. Inform the family representative/caretaker of their right to file an FMNP complaint. B. Assist the complainant in completing the FMNP Complaint Form when requested, including the following: 1. The complainant’s contact information. 2. Incident information. a. Date and time the incident occurred. b. Incident description, including all pertinent details such as farm or farmer’s name, market name, market location, market manager name, etc. c. Desired outcome. C. Inform the family representative/caretaker of their right to file a complaint if discrimination is alleged or suspected. Refer to WPPM 510-40. D. Submit the completed complaint form to CDPH/WIC at WIC@cdph.ca.gov. E. Confirm within five business days that CDPH/WIC received the complaint and follow up as directed. F. Retain the complaint for review and audit for three years following the final payment of the contract. AUTHORITY: 7 CFR §248.7 CROSS REFERENCE: WPPM 510-40 Complaints of Discrimination FMNP Complaint Form

Yes 354* Celiac Disease P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Also known as: Celiac Sprue, Gluten-sensitive Enteropathy, Non-tropical Sprue. An autoimmune disease precipitated by the ingestion of gluten (a protein in wheat, rye, and barley), resulting in damage to the small intestine and malabsorption of the nutrients from food. Yes 355* Lactose Intolerance P – I B – I N – VI I – I C – III The syndrome of one or more of the following: diarrhea, abdominal pain, flatulence, and/or bloating, that occurs after lactose ingestion. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 14 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 356* Hypoglycemia P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Presence of hypoglycemia. Hypoglycemia can occur as a complication of diabetes, as a condition in itself, in association with other disorders, or under certain conditions such as early pregnancy, prolonged fasting, or long periods of strenuous exercise. Yes 357 Drug Nutrient Interactions P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Use of prescription or over-the-counter drugs or medications that have been shown to interfere with nutrient intake, absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion, to an extent that nutritional status is compromised. Yes 358* Eating Disorders P – I B – I N – III Eating disorders are characterized by severe disturbances in a person’s eating behaviors and related thoughts and emotions. Eating disorders include, but are not limited to: anorexia nervosa (AN), bulimia nervosa (BN), and binge-eating disorder (BED). Yes 359* Recent Major Surgery, Trauma, Burns P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Major surgery (includes C-sections), physical trauma or burns severe enough to compromise nutritional status. Yes

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 15 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 360* Other Medical Conditions P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Diseases or conditions with nutritional implications that are not included in any of the other medical conditions. Current condition, or treatment for the condition, must be severe enough to affect nutritional status. May include, but are not limited to: juvenile ideopathic arthritis (JIA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), cardiovascular disease, persistent asthma (moderate or severe) requiring daily medication, cystic fibrosis. Yes 361* Mental Illnesses P – I B – I N – VI Presence of mental illnesses where the current condition, or treatment for the condition, may affect nutrition status. These include, but are not limited to: depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), personality disorders, schizophrenia, anxiety disorders, obessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), bipolar disorders, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Note: For mental illnesses related to eating disorders (e.g., anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa and binge-eating disorder), please see risk #358 Eating Disorders. No 362 Developmental, Sensory, or Motor Disabilities Interfering with Ability to Eat P – I B – I N – III I – I C – III Developmental, sensory, or motor disabilities interfering with ability to eat, restricting the ability to chew or swallow food, or requiring tube feeding to meet nutritional needs. May include, but are not limited to: minimal brain function, feeding problems due to developmental delay, head trauma, brain damage or birth injury. Yes

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 16 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 363* Pre-Diabetes B – I N – III Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and/or impaired glucose tolerance (IGT). Yes 371 Nicotine and Tobacco use P – I B – I N – VI Use of any product which contains nicotine and/or tobacco to include but not limited to cigarettes, pipes, cigars, electronic nicotine delivery systems (e.g. e-cigarettes, vaping devices), hookahs, smokeless tobacco (e.g. chewing tobacco, snuff, dissolvables), or nicotine replacement therapies (e.g. gums, patches). No 372 Alcohol and Substance Use P – I B – I N – III Pregnant Alcohol Use: Any alcohol use. Substance Use: • Any illegal substance use and/or abuse of prescription medications. • Any marijuana use in any form. Breastfeeding and Non-Breastfeeding: Alcohol Use: • High Risk: Routine drinking of ≥ 8 drinks/week or ≥ 4 drinks/day. • Binge: Routine consumption of ≥ 4 drinks within 2 hours. Substance Use: • Any illegal substance use and/or abuse of prescription medications. • Any marijuana use in any form (breastfeeding participants only). Yes

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 17 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 381* Oral Health Condition P – I B – I N – VI I – I C – III Includes but not limited to: tooth decay, periodontal disease, gingivitis, tooth loss, ineffectively replaced teeth or oral infections that impair the ability to ingest food in adequate quantity or quality. No 382* Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders P – I B – I N – VI I – I C – III A group of conditions that can occur in a person whose mother consumed alcohol during pregnancy. Encompasses a range of possible diagnoses, including fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), partial fetal alcohol syndrome (pFAS), alcohol-related birth defects (ARBD), alcohol-related neurodevelopmental disorder (ARND), and neurobehavioral disorder associated with prenatal alcohol exposure (ND-PAE). Yes For I and C only 383* Neonatal Abstinence Syndrome I – I A drug withdrawal syndrome that occurs among drug-exposed infants as a result of the parent’s use of drugs during pregnancy. Yes

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 18 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 400 Risk Series: DIET – Presumed Eligibility for Women and Children Ages 2-5 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 401 Failure to Meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans P – IV B – IV N – VI C – V Pregnant, breastfeeding, and non-breastfeeding participants and children age two to five years may be presumed to be at nutrition risk based on inability to meet Dietary Guidelines for Americans as defined by consuming fewer than the recommended number of servings from one or more of the basic food groups. This risk may only be assigned after a complete nutrition assessment has been performed and no other risks have been identified. No 411 Risk Series: DIET – Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Infants USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 411.1 Routinely using a substitute(s) for human milk or for FDA approved iron- fortified formula as the primary nutrient source during the first year of life. I – IV Examples of substitutes: • Low iron formula without iron supplementation. • Cow’s milk, goat’s milk, or sheep’s milk (whole, reduced fat, low-fat, skim), canned evaporated or sweetened condensed milk. • Imitation or substitute milks (like rice- or soy-based beverages, non- dairy creamer), or other “homemade concoctions”. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 19 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 411.2 Routinely using nursing bottles or cups improperly I – IV • Using a bottle to feed fruit juice. • Feeding any sugar-containing fluids, such as soda/soft drinks, gelatin water, corn syrup solutions, and sweetened tea. • Allowing the infant to fall asleep or be put to bed with a bottle at naps or bedtime. • Allowing the infant to use the bottle without restriction (e.g., walking around with a bottle) or as a pacifier. • Propping the bottle when feeding. • Allowing an infant to carry around and drink throughout the day from a covered or training cup. • Adding any food (cereal or other solid foods) to the infant’s bottle. No 411.3 Routinely offering complementary foods or other substances that are inappropriate in type or timing I – IV • Adding sweet agents such as sugar, honey, or syrups to any beverage (including water) or prepared food, or used on a pacifier. • Introducing any food or beverage other than human milk or iron- fortified infant formula before 6 months of age, such as tea, rice water, or infant cereal. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 20 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 411.4 Routinely using feeding practices that disregard the developmental needs or stage of the infant I – IV • Inability to recognize, insensitivity to, or disregarding the infant’s cues for hunger and satiety (e.g., forcing an infant to eat a type and/or amount of food or beverage or ignoring hunger cues). • Feeding foods of inappropriate consistency, size, or shape that put infants at risk of choking. • Not supporting an infant’s growing independence with self-feeding (e.g., solely spoon-feeding an infant who is able and ready to finger- feed and/or try self-feeding with appropriate utensils). • Feeding an infant food with inappropriate texture based on his/her developmental stage (e.g., feeding primarily pureed or liquid foods when the infant is ready and capable of eating mashed, chopped or appropriate finger foods). No 411.5 Feeding foods to an infant that could be contaminated with harmful microorganisms or toxins I – IV Potentially harmful foods: • Unpasteurized fruit or vegetable juice. • Unpasteurized dairy products or soft cheeses such as feta, Brie, Camembert, blue-veined, and Mexican-style cheese. • Honey (added to liquids or solid foods, used in cooking, as part of processed foods, on a pacifier, etc). • Raw or undercooked meat, fish, poultry, or eggs. • Raw vegetable sprouts (alfalfa, clover, bean, and radish). • Deli meats, hot dogs, and processed meats (avoid unless heated until steaming hot). • Donor human milk acquired directly from individuals or the Internet. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 21 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 411.6 Routinely feeding inappropriately diluted formula I – IV • Failure to follow manufacturer’s dilution instructions (to include stretching formula for household economic reasons). • Failure to follow specific instructions accompanying a prescription. No 411.7 Routinely limiting the frequency of nursing of the exclusively breastfed infant when human milk is the sole source of nutrients I – IV Examples of inappropriate frequency of nursing: • Scheduled feedings instead of demand feedings. • Less than 8 feedings in 24 hours if less than 2 months old. No 411.8 Routinely feeding a diet very low in calories and/or essential nutrients I – IV Examples: • Strict vegan diet • Macrobiotic diet • Other diets very low in calories and/or essential nutrients No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 22 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 411.9 Routinely using inappropriate sanitation in preparation, handling, and storage of expressed human milk or formula I – IV Limited or no access to a: • Safe water supply (documented by appropriate officials). • Heat source for sterilization. • Refrigerator or freezer for storage. Failure to properly prepare, handle, or store bottles or storage containers of expressed breast milk or formula; examples include: Human Milk • Thawing/heating in a microwave. • Refreezing. • Adding freshly expressed unrefrigerated human milk to frozen human milk. • Adding freshly pumped chilled human milk to frozen human milk in an amount that is greater than the amount of frozen human milk. • Feeding thawed refrigerated human milk more than 24 hours after it was thawed. • Saving human milk from a used bottle for another feeding. • Failure to clean breast pump per manufacturer’s instructions. • Feeding donor human milk acquired directly from individuals or the Internet. Formula • Failure to prepare and/or store formula per manufacturer’s or physician instructions. • Storing at room temperature for more than 1 hour. • Using formula in a bottle one hour after the start of a feeding. • Saving formula from a used bottle for another feeding. • Failure to clean baby bottle properly. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 23 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 411.10 Feeding dietary supplements with potentially harmful consequences I – IV Examples of dietary supplements which, when fed in excess of recommended dosage, may be toxic or have harmful consequences: • Single or multi-vitamins • Mineral supplementations • Herbal or botanical supplements/remedies/teas. No 411.11 Routinely not providing dietary supplements recognized as essential by national public health policy when an infant’s diet alone cannot meet nutrient requirements I – IV • Infants who are 6 months of age or older who are ingesting less than 0.25 mg of fluoride daily when the water supply contains less than 0.3 ppm fluoride. • Infants who are exclusively breastfed, or who are ingesting less than 1 liter (or 1 quart) per day of vitamin-D fortified formula, and are not taking a supplement of 400 IU of vitamin D. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 24 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 425 Risk Series: DIET – Inappropriate Nutrition Care Practices for Children USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 425.1 Routinely feeding inappropriate beverages as the primary milk source C – V Examples of inappropriate beverages as primary milk source: • Non-fat or reduced-fat milks (between 12 and 24 months of age only) or sweetened condensed milk. • Goat’s milk, sheep’s milk, or unfortified or inadequately fortified substitute milks (such as unfortified rice, almond or soy based beverages, non-dairy creamer, or homemade concoctions). No 425.2 Routinely feeding a child any sugar- containing fluids C – V Examples of sugar-containing fluids: soda/soft drinks, gelatin water, corn syrup solutions, sweetened tea. No 425.3 Routinely using nursing bottles, cups, or pacifiers improperly C – V • Using a bottle to feed fruit juice, diluted cereal or other solid foods. • Allowing the child to fall asleep or be put to bed with a bottle at naps or bedtime. • Allowing the child to use the bottle without restriction (e.g., walking around with a bottle) or as a pacifier. • Using a bottle for feeding or drinking after 14 months of age. • Using a pacifier dipped in sweet agents (e.g., sugar, honey, syrups). • Allowing a child to carry around and drink throughout the day from a covered or training cup. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 25 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 425.4 Routinely using feeding practices that disregard the developmental needs or stage of the child C – V • Inability to recognize, insensitivity to, or disregarding the child’s cues for hunger and satiety (e.g., forcing a child to eat a certain type and/or amount of food or beverage or ignoring a hungry child’s requests for appropriate foods). • Feeding foods of inappropriate consistency, size, or shape that put children at risk of choking. • Not supporting a child’s need for growing independence with self- feeding (e.g., solely spoon-feeding a child who is able and ready to finger-feed and/or try self-feeding with appropriate utensils). • Feeding a child food with an inappropriate texture based on his/her developmental stage (e.g., feeding primarily pureed or liquid food when the child is ready and capable of eating mashed, chopped or appropriate finger foods). No 425.5 Feeding foods to a child that could be contaminated with harmful microorganisms C – V Examples of potentially harmful foods for a child: • Unpasteurized fruit or vegetable juice. • Unpasteurized dairy products or soft cheeses such as feta, Brie, Camembert, blue-veined, and Mexican-style cheese. • Raw or undercooked meat, fish, poultry, or eggs. • Raw vegetable sprouts (alfalfa, clover, bean, and radish). • Deli meats, hot dogs, and processed meats (avoid unless heated until steaming hot). No 425.6 Routinely feeding a diet very low in calories and/or essential nutrients C – V • Vegan diet • Macrobiotic diet • Other diets very low in calories and/or essential nutrients No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 26 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 425.7 Feeding dietary supplements with potentially harmful consequences C – V Examples of dietary supplements which, when fed in excess of recommended dosage, may be toxic or have harmful consequences include but may not be limited to: single or multi-vitamins, minerals supplements, herbal or botanical supplements/remedies/teas No 425.8 Not providing dietary supplements recognized as essential by national public health policy when a child’s diet alone cannot meet requirements C – V • Providing children under 36 months of age less than 0.25 mg of fluoride daily when the water supply contains less than 0.3 ppm fluoride. • Providing children 36-60 months of age less than 0.50 mg of fluoride daily when the water supply contains less than 0.3 ppm fluoride. • Not providing 400 IU of vitamin D if a child consumes less than 1 liter (or 1 quart) of vitamin D fortified milk or formula. No 425.9 Routine ingestion by child of nonfood items (pica) C – V • Ashes • Carpet fibers • Cigarettes or cigarette butts • Clay • Dust • Foam rubber • Paint chips • Soil • Starch (laundry and cornstarch No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 27 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 427 Risk Series: DIET – Inappropriate Nutrition Care Practices for Women USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 427.1 Consuming dietary supplements with potentially harmful consequences P – IV B – IV N – VI Examples of dietary supplements which, when ingested in excess of recommended dosage, may be toxic or have harmful consequences: • Single or multi-vitamins • Mineral supplements • Herbal or botanical supplements/remedies/teas • Cannabidiol (CBD), for Pregnant and Breastfeeding participants only (Products labeled as CBD with any form of THC should be a risk with 372) No 427.2 Consuming diets very low in calories/ nutrients; impaired intake/absorption after bariatic surgery P – IV B – IV N – VI • Low-calorie diet • Strict vegan diet • Any other diet restricting calories and/or essential nutrients No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 28 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 427.3 Compulsively ingesting non-food items (pica) P – IV B – IV N – VI • Dirt • Starch (laundry and cornstarch) • Large quantities of ice and/or freezer frost • Cigarette ashes • Baking soda • Burnt matches • Coffee grounds • Chalk • Uncooked rice • Clay • Paper No 427.4 Inadequate vitamin/mineral supplementation P – IV B – IV N – VI • Consumption of less than 27 mg of iron as a supplement daily by a pregnant participant. • Consumption of less than 150 mcg of supplemental iodine per day by pregnant and breastfeeding participants. • Consumption of less than 400-800 mcg of folic acid from supplements daily by pregnant, breastfeeding, and non-breastfeeding participants. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 29 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 427.5 Pregnant woman ingesting foods that could be contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms P – IV Potentially harmful foods: • Seafood: Any raw or undercooked fish, or shellfish, or food containing raw or undercooked seafood, e.g., sashimi, found in some sushi or ceviche; Refrigerated smoked fish; Partially cooked seafood, such as shrimp and crab. • Raw or undercooked meat or poultry. • Hot dogs, luncheon meats (cold cuts), fermented and dry sausage and other deli-style meat or poultry products unless reheated until steaming hot. • Pâtés: Unpasteurized, refrigerated pâté or meat spreads. • Deli Salads: Deli Salads prepared without preservatives in a deli-type store or restaurant. • Unpasteurized milk or foods containing unpasteurized milk. • Soft cheeses made with unpasteurized milk such as feta, Brie, Camembert, blue-veined cheeses and Mexican style cheeses such as queso blanco or queso fresco. • Eggs: Raw or undercooked eggs or foods containing raw or lightly cooked eggs including certain salad dressings (Ceasar), cookie and cake batters, sauces, and beverages such as unpasteurized eggnog. • Raw sprouts (alfalfa, bean, radish, microgreens). • Unpasteurized fruit or vegetable juices. • Unwashed fruits and vegetables. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 30 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 428 Risk Series: DIET – Presumed Eligibility for Infants and Children < 2 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 428 Dietary Risk Associated with Complementary Feeding Practices I – IV (>4 mo) C – V (<24 mo) An infant or child who has begun to or is expected to begin to: 1. consume complementary foods and beverages. 2. eat independently. 3. be weaned from breast milk or infant formula, or 4. transition from a diet based on infant/toddler foods to one based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. A complete nutrition assessment, including for risk #411, Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Infants, or #425, Inappropriate Nutrition Practices for Children, must be completed prior to assigning this risk. No 500 Risk Series: OTHER RISKS – Miscellaneous USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 502 Transfer of Certification P – V B – V N – V I – V C – V Person with current valid Verification of Certification (VOC) card from another State agency. The VOC is valid through the end of the current certification period, even if the participant does not meet the receiving agency’s nutritional risk, priority, or income criteria, or the certification period extends beyond the receiving agency’s certification period for that category, and must be accepted as proof of eligibility for program benefits. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 31 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 600 Risk Series: OTHER RISKS – Breastfeeding Mother/Infant Dyad USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 601 Breastfeeding Mother of Infant at Nutritional Risk P – I, II, or IV B – I, II, or IV A breastfeeding person whose breastfed infant has been determined to be at nutritional risk. No 602 Breastfeeding Complications or Potential Complications (Women) P – I B – I A breastfeeding person with any of the following: • Severe breast engorgement • Recurrent plugged ducts • Mastitis (fever or flu-like symptoms with localized breast tenderness) • Flat or inverted nipples • Cracked, bleeding or severely sore nipples • Age ≥ 40 years • Failure of milk to come in by 4 days postpartum • Tandem nursing (breastfeeding two siblings who are not twins) No 603 Breastfeeding Complications or Potential Complications (Infants) I - I A breastfeeding infant with any of the following complications or potential complications: • Jaundice • Weak or ineffective suck • Difficulty latching onto parent’s breast/chest • Inadequate stooling (for age, as determined by a physician or other health care professional), and/or less than 6 wet diapers per day. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 32 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 700 Risk Series: OTHER RISKS – Infant of a WIC-eligible Mother USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 701 Infant up to 6 months old of WIC mother or of a woman who would have been eligible during pregnancy I – II (< 6 mo) An infant < 6 month of age whose parent was a WIC Program participant during pregnancy or whose parent’s medical records document that the person was at nutritional risk during pregnancy because of detrimental or abnormal nutritional conditions detectable by biochemical or anthropometric measurements or other documented nutritionally related medical conditions. No 702 Breastfeeding infant of woman at nutritional risk I – I or IV Breastfeeding infant of person at nutritional risk. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 33 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 800 Risk Series: OTHER RISKS – Homeless/Migrant USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 801 Homelessness P – IV B – IV N – VI I – IV C – V A pregnant/postpartum individual, infant or child who lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence; or whose primary nighttime residence is: • A supervised publicly or privately operated shelter (including a welfare hotel, a congregate shelter, or a shelter for victims of domestic violence) designed to provide temporary living accommodations. • An institution that provides a temporary residence for individuals intended to be institutionalized. • A temporary accommodation of not more than 365 days in the residence of another individual, or • A public or private place not designed for, or ordinarily used as, a regular sleeping accommodation. No 802 Migrancy P – IV B – IV N – VI I – IV C – V Categorically eligible pregnant, breastfeeding, and non-breastfeeding participants, infants, and children who are members of families which contain at least one individual whose principal employment is in agriculture on a seasonal basis, who has been so employed within the last 24 months, and who establishes, for the purposes of such employment, a temporary abode. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 34 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 900 Risk Series: OTHER RISKS – Environmental USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 901 Recipient of abuse P – IV B – IV N – VI I – IV C – V An individual who has experienced physical, sexual, emotional, economic, or psychological maltreatment that may frighten, intimidate, terrorize, manipulate, hurt, humiliate, blame, injure, and/or wound the individual. The experience of abuse may be self-reported by the individual, an individual’s family member, or reported by a social worker, healthcare provider, or other appropriate personnel. Types of abuse relevant to the WIC population include, but are not limited to: • Domestic violence: abuse committed by a current or former family or household member or intimate partner. • Intimate partner violence (IPV): a form of domestic violence committed by a current or former intimate partner (i.e., spouse, boyfriend/girlfriend, dating partner, or ongoing sexual partner) that may include physical violence, sexual violence, stalking, and/or psychological aggression (including coercive tactics). • Child abuse and/or neglect: any act or failure to act that results in harm to a child or puts a child at risk of harm. Child abuse may be physical (including shaken baby syndrome), sexual, or emotional abuse or neglect of an infant or child under the age of 18 by a parent, caretaker, or other person in a custodial role (such as a religious leader, coach, or teacher). No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 35 of 36 Oct 1, 2025 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 902 Woman or infant/child of primary caregiver with limited ability to make feeding decisions and/or prepare food P – IV B – IV N – IV I – IV C – V Person (pregnant, breastfeeding, or non-breastfeeding) or infant/child whose primary caregiver is assessed to have a limited ability to make appropriate feeding decisions and/or prepare food. Examples may include a person or an infant/child of caregiver with the following: • Documentation or self-report of misuse of alcohol, use of illegal substances, use of marijuana, or misuse of prescription medications. • Mental illness, including clinical depression (diagnosed by a physician or psychologist, or as self-reported). • Intellectual disability (diagnosed by a physician or psychologist, or as self-reported). • Physical disability which restricts or limits food preparation abilities. • ≤ 17 years of age. No 903 Foster Care P – IV B – IV N – VI I – IV C – V Entering the foster care system during the previous six months or moving from one foster care home to another foster care home during the previous six months. Cannot be used for consecutive certifications while the child remains in the same foster home. It should be used as the sole risk criterion only if careful assessment of the applicant’s status indicates that no other risks based on anthropometric, medical or nutritional risk criteria can be identified. No

Nutritional Risks Criteria and Descriptions WPPM #960-01 Job Aid

Revised Oct 1, 2025 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 36 of 36 USDA Code Risk Criteria Category Priority Definition and Cutoff High Risk 904 Environmental Tobacco Smoke Exposure P – I B – I N – VI I – I C – III Exposure to smoke from tobacco products inside enclosed areas, such as the home, place of child care, etc. ETS is also known as passive, secondhand, or involuntary smoke. ETS definition also includes the exposure to the aerosol from electronic nicotine delivery systems. No *Condition diagnosed by a physician and self-reported by the applicant/participant/caregiver, or as reported or documented by a physician or someone working under a physician’s orders.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 16 August 25, 2025 Glossary Navigation Links: A B C D E F H I L M N O P Q R S T V W A • Alcohol and Drug Abuse referral is the referral to treatment programs, clinics, counselors, or other drug abuse professionals, and the provision of educational materials related to alcohol and drug use. • American Indian or Alaska Native is an individual with origins in any of the original peoples of North, Central, and South America, including, for example, Navajo Nation, Blackfeet Tribe of the Blackfeet Indian Reservation of Montana, Native Village of Barrow Inupiat Traditional Government, Nome Eskimo Community, Aztec, and Maya. • Annual income is defined as the total cash income before taxes, from all sources (i.e., gross income), received by all members of the household at different frequencies throughout the last 12 months, and converted to an annual amount by WIC WISE. • Anticipatory guidance is the counseling technique in which healthcare professionals provide parents or caregivers with information about healthy lifestyle practices for decision-making that promotes injury and disease prevention. • Applicants are pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum individuals, infants, and children under age 5 who are applying to receive WIC benefits. Applicants include individuals who are currently participating in the program but are re- applying because their certification period has expired. • Asian is an individual with origins in any of the original peoples of Central or East Asia, Southeast Asia, or South Asia, including, for example, Chinese, Asian Indian, Filipino, Vietnamese, Korean, and Japanese. Back to Glossary Navigation B • Biochemical results include hemoglobin, hematocrit, or lead screening test values, also known as blood work.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 2 of 16 August 25, 2025 • Black or African American is an individual with origins in any of the Black racial groups of Africa, including, for example, African American, Jamaican, Haitian, Nigerian, Ethiopian, and Somali. • Breastfeeding category is a participant up to one year following the end of pregnancy, who is breastfeeding, chestfeeding, and/or providing their breastmilk to their infant on the average of at least once per day. This definition includes chestfeeding in the WPPM. Breastfeeding category includes: I. Fully Breastfeeding is a breastfeeding participant whose infant does not receive food benefits for formula from the WIC Program. II. Breastfeeding Partially Mostly is a mostly breastfeeding participant whose infant does not receive more than the maximum amount of formula allowed for partially breastfed infants. III. Breastfeeding Partially Some is a partially breastfeeding participant whose infant is receiving more than the maximum amount of formula allowed for a mostly breastfed infant. The participant’s certification continues past six months, up to one year, as long as the participant’s breastmilk is provided to an infant. The participant’s food benefits will be the same as a non- breastfeeding participant. The participant will not receive food benefits after the sixth month from the delivery date. As long as the participant continues to provide breastmilk, they will be considered an active WIC participant with other program benefits such as breastfeeding support and nutrition education. • Breastfeeding Peer Counseling (BFPC) Program is based on the USDA WIC Breastfeeding Model Components for Peer Counseling. The BFPC Program utilizes peers to encourage and support WIC participants to breastfeed their infants via a peer-to-peer connection. The BFPC Program is an enhancement to the WIC Program breastfeeding services and support. Back to Glossary Navigation C • California Children’s Services (CCS) is a program that covers specific medical services and equipment provided by CCS-approved specialists for children with certain physical limitations and chronic health conditions or diseases. • California Immunization Registry (CAIR) is California's statewide immunization registry network.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 3 of 16 August 25, 2025 • Card stock is a box(es) of WIC Cards intended for electronic food benefit issuances activated through WIC WISE. • Caretaker is an individual designated by a participant or family representative to act on their behalf and documented in WIC WISE. The caretaker may be the other parent or a person who has detailed knowledge of the nutrition, health, breastfeeding status, and family history of the participant(s). • Cash-value benefit (CVB) is a fixed-dollar amount included with WIC food benefits that can be used by a participant to obtain authorized fruits and vegetables. • Certification is the implementation of criteria and procedures to assess and document each applicant's eligibility for the WIC program. This includes initial certification and recertifications. • Chestfeeding is an inclusive term or alternate description for the act of feeding a baby milk from the chest, often referred to as breastfeeding. Individuals who chestfeed provide their chestmilk to their infant. It is an implied alternate description of breastfeeding in the WPPM. • Child abuse at the minimum, is any recent act or failure to act on the part of a parent or caretaker, which results in death, serious physical or emotional harm, sexual abuse or exploitation, or an act or failure to act which presents an imminent risk of serious harm. Please refer to federal law 42 U.S.C. 5101 for more information on child abuse. • Child(ren) are persons who have had their first birthday but have not reached the fifth birthday. • Children’s Presumptive Eligibility (CPE) allows certain health care providers to approve temporary health coverage for eligible child applicants using an electronic application and is based on their family's self-attestation of facts. CPE provides immediate temporary, full-scope benefits on a fee-for-service basis for up to 60 days for those who qualify. • Combination feeding is meeting an infant's nutritional needs with breastmilk and formula. • Competent Professional Authority (CPA) is a local agency staff member authorized to determine nutritional risk and prescribe supplemental foods. This includes the Registered Dietitian (RD), Registered Dietitian Eligible (RDE), Registration Eligible Nutritionist (REN), Dietetic Technician Registered (DTR),

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 4 of 16 August 25, 2025 Degreed Nutritionist (DN), Mastered Degreed Nutritionist (MDN), WIC Nutrition Assistant (WNA), Registered Nurse (RN), Physician Assistant (PA), and Physician (MD). • Confer is the method for verifying adjunct eligibility by the CalWORKs eligibility of another family member or by Medi-Cal eligibility of pregnant or infant family member who is not currently participating in the WIC program. • Confidential information is any information about an applicant or participant, whether it is obtained from an individual, another source, or generated as a result of contact with WIC, that individually identifies an applicant, participant, or family member(s). • Contact is a session meeting the requirements of the specific program to provide nutrition education or breastfeeding services to a participant (note: based on program specific rules and requirements apply). • Contract is an enforceable written agreement between two or more competent parties, with the elements of the contract being offer, acceptance, consideration, compliance with all applicable terms and conditions. • Contract formula is all standard cow milk- and/or soy-based infant formulas produced by the manufacturers awarded the infant formula rebate contracts and issued under those contracts. A list of WIC contract formulas can be viewed on the CA WIC Infant Formula webpage. • Critical thinking skills is the process of gathering and organizing information to evaluate and prioritize it appropriately. As part of the nutrition assessment process, these skills allow staff to collect all the necessary information before deciding upon the best course of action. • Current income is defined as the total cash income before taxes, from all sources (i.e., gross income), received by the household during the month (28-31 days) prior to the date the application for WIC benefits is made. Back to Glossary Navigation D • Documented immunization record is defined as a record (digital or paper) which provides a history of all vaccines received by an individual and in which the actual vaccination dates are recorded. This includes the paper immunization record (from the provider), i.e., the yellow "California Immunization Record" (PM

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 5 of 16 August 25, 2025 298/IMM-75), an immunization registry (CAIR), an automated data system, or a client chart (digital or paper copy). • Drugs are natural or synthetic substances that can have a physiological effect when introduced to the body. Drugs can include alcohol, prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, controlled substances, and controlled substance analogues. Refer to federal law 21 U.S.C. 802 for more information on substances. Back to Glossary Navigation E • Electronic contact is providing nutrition education using telehealth or electronic media, including computer-based technology, such as kiosks, computer software, and internet media. • Emergency and/or disaster situation is an event that threatens to or has already interrupted the provision of WIC services to participants for more than 24 hours. Examples of these types of events include: A. Natural disasters or catastrophes such as floods, wildfires, or earthquakes; B. Criminally induced emergencies such as shootings, bombings, bomb threats, or arson; and C. Systemic emergencies such as electrical power failures, noxious gas leaks, and toxic waste leaks. • Employee Fraud and Abuse is the intentional conduct of a State or WIC local agency employee that violates program regulations, policies, or procedures including but not limited to, misappropriating or altering food benefits or cash- value benefits, entering false or misleading information in participant case records, or creating a fictitious participant record in WIC WISE. Back to Glossary Navigation F • Family Representative is an individual, assigned in WIC WISE, who receives the WIC food benefits and performs all requirements on behalf of themselves, infants, and child(ren) participants. This can be a pregnant or postpartum

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 6 of 16 August 25, 2025 applicant, natural or adoptive parent, foster parent, or a non-parental adult with temporary or permanent guardianship of an infant or child. • Fixed (permanent) site is a site that is solely designated for WIC services (e.g., a room or suite of rooms in a health center or business mall). • Food Delivery System is the method used by state and local agencies to provide supplemental foods to participants. • Food instrument (FI) is the WIC Card, which is used by a participant to obtain supplemental foods. • Food Package or Food Prescription is a combination of WIC-authorized foods that are issued to a participant based on the participant’s category, age, and nutritional need. • Full-time site is defined as a site that is open 32-40 hours per week or more. Back to Glossary Navigation H • High risk is a designation of a participant based on the nutrition risk condition(s). A participant designated as “high risk” is identified through biochemical results, anthropometric measurements, or other nutritionally related medical issues. The nutrition services associated with “high risk” include a care plan and the provision of nutrition services by a registered dietitian or dietitian nutritionist (or other professional). • Hispanic or Latino is an individual of Mexican, Puerto Rican, Salvadoran, Cuban, Dominican, Guatemalan, and other Central or South American or Spanish culture or origin. • Homeless is defined as an applicant/participant who: A. Lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence, or B. Has a primary nighttime residence that is: 1. a public or private shelter, including a welfare hotel, a congregate shelter, or a shelter for domestic violence designated to provide temporary living accommodation, 2. an institution that provides temporary residence for individuals intended to be institutionalized,

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 7 of 16 August 25, 2025 3. a temporary accommodation of not more than 365 days in the residence of another individual, or 4. a public or private place not designated for, or ordinarily used as, a regular accommodation for human beings. • Household Size is defined as the family unit/size, which is a group of related or non-related individuals who live together as one household/economic unit. These individuals share income and consumption of goods or services. Back to Glossary Navigation I • Income for the purposes of WIC means gross cash income before deductions for income taxes, employees' social security taxes, insurance premiums, bonds, etc., from all sources, received by all members of the household. • Independent research regardless of funding source, includes research activities, as well as the drafting or creation of articles, reports, and/or other materials, that are not necessary for the performance of the WIC Local Agency Agreement and are conducted and/or produced by the local agency using data obtained directly from WIC applicants or participants, WIC staff, and/or WIC vendors through a variety of means, including but not limited to surveys, focus groups, and/or interviews, or indirectly using the CDPH/WIC authorized management information system. • Infant is a person under 1 year of age, including the breastfed infant of a breastfeeding participant. • In-state transfer is the reassignment of a certified participant from one local agency to another within California. • Intent is when a participant deliberately commits or willfully engages in a participation violation and is presumed to intend the result of that action if the result was substantially certain to occur. • Issuance: A. Single Issuance is providing food benefits to the participant for the current month. B. Double Issuance is providing food benefits to the participant for the current month and the next month.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 8 of 16 August 25, 2025 C. Triple Issuance is providing food benefits to the participant for the current month and the two following months. Back to Glossary Navigation L • Legitimate purpose is a fully justified written request made by a person or organization to view specific non-confidential WIC record(s) for which there is a general public interest or reason to view such records. • Local agency is: A. A public or private, nonprofit health or human service agency that provides health services, either directly or through contract, B. An Indian Health Service (IHS) unit; C. An Indian tribe, band, or group recognized by the Department of the Interior which operates a health clinic or is provided health services by an IHS service unit; or D. An intertribal council or group that is an authorized representative of Indian tribes, bands, or groups recognized by the Department of the Interior, which operates a health clinic or is provided health services by an IHS service unit. Back to Glossary Navigation M • Managed care plans (MCPs) are a type of health insurance that contracts with healthcare providers and medical facilities to provide care for health insurance members at negotiated reduced costs. There are three types of managed care plans: health maintenance organizations (HMO), preferred provider organizations (PPO), and point of service (POS). • Mandated reporter is a person who is required by law to report suspected or known instances of child abuse or neglect to the proper authorities. This includes all WIC employees who have direct contact with participants or applicants, or have reasonable suspicion through other channels, while performing WIC functions and duties. • Medical documentation is a determination by a licensed health care provider authorized to write medical prescriptions under state law that the participant has

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 9 of 16 August 25, 2025 a qualifying medical condition that dictates the use of WIC supplemental foods, and/or therapeutic formula(s) because the use of conventional foods is precluded or restricted. • Medi-Cal Managed Care (MMC) refers to healthcare services provided through established networks of organized systems of care that emphasize primary and preventive care. • Medi-Cal Rx is a program that provides prescription drug coverage and related services to all individuals enrolled in Medi-Cal. The program supports cost savings for drug purchases made by the state, standardizes pharmacy benefits statewide for Medi-Cal members, and improves overall access to pharmacy services by utilizing a broader fee-for-service delivery system. • Medical supervision is ongoing medical oversight and instruction for the dietary management of the participant’s health conditions identified by the participant’s health care provider. • Middle Eastern or Northern African is an individual with origins in any of the original peoples of the Middle East or North Africa, including, for example, Lebanese, Iranian, Egyptian, Syrian, Iraqi, and Israeli. • Migrant farmworkers and their family members are defined by federal regulation as individuals whose principal employment (over 50 percent) is in agriculture on a seasonal basis, who have been so employed within the last 24 months, and who establish a temporary residence for the purpose of such employment. • Mobile site is a site that is inside a mobile van or other vehicle. Back to Glossary Navigation N • Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander is an individual with origins in any of the original peoples of Hawaii, Guam, Samoa, or other Pacific Islands, including, for example, Native Hawaiian, Samoan, Chamorro, Tongan, Fijian, and Marshallese. • Non-breastfeeding category is a participant that is meeting an infant's nutritional needs with only infant formula. This includes postpartum participants up to 6 months after the end of a pregnancy due to perinatal loss or adoption.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 10 of 16 August 25, 2025 • Nutrition assessment is the process of collecting and prioritizing relevant information to identify risks using approved assessment tools in order to offer learner-centered education to the participant. This process also includes documenting the contact and following up as needed to monitor progress and promote continuity of care. • Nutrition education is an individual or group sessions using various delivery mediums and materials designed to improve health status and achieve positive change in dietary, physical activity habits and health that meet the cultural preferences of the individual. • Nutrition risk is defined as: A. Detrimental or abnormal nutritional conditions detectable by biochemical or anthropometric measures; B. Other documented nutritionally related medical conditions; C. Dietary deficiencies that impair or endanger health; D. Conditions that directly affect the nutritional health of a person, including alcoholism or drug abuse; or E. Conditions that predispose persons to inadequate nutritional patterns or nutritionally related medical conditions, including, but not limited to, homelessness and migrancy. • Nutrition services are services provided to participants to improve nutritional status including supplemental food, nutrition education, referral to needed services, and breastfeeding support and education appropriate for the category and age of the participant. • Nutrition tailoring is the customization of the WIC food package, based on a complete nutrition assessment, by making substitutions, reductions, and/or eliminations to the supplemental food type or form to accommodate special dietary needs, cultural practices, and/or personal preferences. The provision of less than the maximum monthly allowances (MMA) of supplemental foods to a participant is appropriate only when: A. Medically or nutritionally warranted (e.g., to eliminate a food due to a food allergy); B. A participant refuses or cannot use the maximum monthly allowances, or chooses to take less than the maximum monthly allowance; or

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 11 of 16 August 25, 2025 C. The quantities necessary to supplement another program's contribution to fill a medical prescription would be less than the maximum monthly allowances. Back to Glossary Navigation O • Other harmful substances include tobacco, prescription drugs, and over-the- counter medications that may be harmful to the health of the WIC population, especially pregnant individuals and fetuses. • Out-of-state transfer is the reassignment of a certified participant into California from another state, or out of California to another state. • Overseas transfer is the reassignment of a certified participant into California from the WIC Overseas Program, or to the WIC Overseas Program from California. Back to Glossary Navigation P • Paraprofessionals are individuals without extended professional training in health, nutrition, or the clinical management of breastfeeding who are selected from the group to be served and are trained and given ongoing supervision to provide a basic service or function. Paraprofessionals provide specific tasks within a defined scope of practice. They assist professionals but are not licensed or credentialed as healthcare, nutrition, or lactation consultant professionals. • Participant is an individual who meets all program eligibility criteria, is enrolled in the WIC program, and receives supplemental foods. • Participant violation is any deliberate action of a participant, family representative, parent, or caretaker of an infant or child participant that violates federal or state statutes, regulations, policies, or procedures governing the program. • Part-time site is a site that is open less than 32 hours per week. • Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is any information maintained by an agency that identifies or describes an individual. This includes an individual’s first and last name in combination with any one or more of the following: A. Social security number

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 12 of 16 August 25, 2025 B. Driver license number or CA ID card number C. Street address or location data D. Physical description E. Account number, credit or debit card number, in combination with any required security code F. Medical information G. Health insurance information H. Phone number I. Employment history J. Information on Medi-Cal, CalFresh, or CalWORKs K. Food instrument issuance data that identifies the individual L. Fair hearing documents that identifies the individual M. Discrimination complaint documents that identify the individual • Postpartum are individuals up to 6 months after birth or termination of pregnancy and up to 12 months if the individual is breastfeeding. • Prenatal or pregnant are individuals with one or more embryos in utero. • Prescriptive authority is a health care professional in California licensed to write medical prescriptions under California state Law. • Presumptive eligibility (PE) is a process in which qualified providers can enroll pregnant individuals and provide immediate, temporary prenatal care to low- income pregnant patients. Pregnant individuals can also be presumptively eligible pending completion of the eligibility determination process to receive CalWORKs. The participant must apply for Medi-Cal for continued coverage within a specified period (60 days), or temporary prenatal care will be terminated under PE. • Public Service Announcements (PSA) are non-commercial advertisements broadcast for the common good through media (i.e., TV, radio, outdoor ads, community newsletters, direct mail, digital media, or websites). Back to Glossary Navigation

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 13 of 16 August 25, 2025 Q • Qualifying medical condition is a health condition, determined by a health care provider, that meets the criteria for receiving medical formula, WIC-eligible nutritionals, state-ordered formula, an increased formula infant food package, or jarred infant fruits and vegetables for children 1 to 5 years of age. Back to Glossary Navigation R • Reasonable suspicion occurs when it is objectively reasonable for a person to suspect abuse based on facts, drawing on their training and experience, to also suspect child abuse. • Rebate is the amount of money refunded under cost containment procedures from the manufacturer of the particular food product as the result of a purchase of the supplemental food with the WIC Card by a participant. • Redeem as related to food delivery, is the process of using the WIC Card to purchase food from a WIC-authorized vendor. • Regional Breastfeeding Liaison (RBL) Program is a program within WIC that facilitates seamless breastfeeding support in the communities where WIC participants live. RBL Program staff establish partnerships with hospitals, healthcare providers, employers, and the breastfeeding support community, and promote WIC and WIC breastfeeding services. RBL services ultimately increase breastfeeding initiation and duration rates in communities by narrowing breastfeeding support gaps. RBLs serve their home local agency and county; additionally, most RBLs serve other WIC local agencies and counties in their regional coverage area. • Regional Centers are nonprofit private corporations that help individuals with developmental disabilities find and access the many services available to them and their families. They pay for a variety of medical services for children and adults who are residents of California and have limited income and resources. • Registered Dietitian (RD) is a food and nutrition expert who has met academic and professional requirements. The RD must possess and maintain the RD credential or the right to use the term "registered dietitian" as approved by the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (AND). The RD role is defined in WPPM 130-10.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 14 of 16 August 25, 2025 • Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) is an alternate role of a food and nutrition expert who has met academic and professional requirements. The RDN must possess and maintain the RDN credential or the right to use the term “registered dietitian nutritionist” as approved by the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (AND). An RDN is an implied alternate role to a Registered Dietitian (RD) in the WPPM. • Relatives are individuals who are within the second degree of marriage and blood, including spouse, parent, children, grandchildren, grandparents, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, niece, nephew, first cousin, stepparent, stepchildren, and stepsister. • Remote Indian or Native Village is an Indian or Native village that A. Is located in a rural area, B. Has a population of less than 5,000 inhabitants, and C. Is not accessible all year by means of a public road. The term public road means any road or street under the jurisdiction of and maintained by a public authority and open to public travel. Back to Glossary Navigation S • Search warrant is a written order issued by a court that permits an individual, such as a police investigator, to access a WIC participant’s confidential information. The LA must comply with the search warrant at the time it is served. Refer to federal law 18 U.S.C. Chapter 205 for more information on search warrants. • Secondary Nutrition Education Contacts (NECs) are conducted by a Competent Professional Authority (CPA) and include education sessions, classes, or nutrition counseling provided to a group, individual, or through an approved online method (wichealth.org). • Short certification is a temporary certification, up to 30 days, for an applicant who was not able to provide the required documents to determine eligibility (residency, income, and identity) at the time of certification or recertification. Short certification includes a temporary 60-day certification period if a pregnant or postpartum participant was not able to provide proof of pregnancy/loss.

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 15 of 16 August 25, 2025 • Site is where WIC services are provided, including certification. Sites can be permanent, part-time, temporary, or mobile. • Standard Non-Contract Formula includes all infant formulas, excluding exempt infant formulas, that are not part of the California WIC infant formula rebate contract. • Subpoena is a legal document issued by a court that requests a local agency staff to testify as a witness at a specified time and place (for a trial, hearing, or deposition), and/or to produce documents, electronically stored information, or other tangible objects in a legal proceeding. Refer to 28 U.S.C. App. Rule 45 for more information on subpoenas. • Supplemental foods are foods containing nutrients determined by nutritional research to be lacking in the diets of pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum individuals, infants, and children, and foods that promote the health of the population served by the WIC Program as indicated by relevant nutrition science, public health concerns, and cultural eating patterns. Back to Glossary Navigation T • Termination is the act of ending WIC program benefits of a participant during the certification period. When a participant does not recertify after their certification period has ended or is at the end of their categorical eligibility (such as a child turning 5 or a breastfeeding participant whose infant is turning 1 year old), WIC WISE will process the termination automatically. • Therapeutic formulas or medical formulas/food are formulas or medical foods administered orally or by tube feeding to infants, children, or women with documented qualifying medical condition(s). Products not allowed are those used solely for the purpose of enhancing nutrient intake or managing body weight (e.g., vitamin pills, weight control products), medicines/drugs, hyperalimentation feedings (nourishment administered through a vein), enzymes, oral rehydration fluids or electrolyte solutions, flavoring agents, and feeding utensils or devices. • Total cash receipts are defined as cash income, taxable or not, that is available to purchase goods and services. Back to Glossary Navigation

GLOSSARY WPPM #970-10

Revised August 25, 2025 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 16 of 16 V • Value Enhanced Nutrition Assessment (VENA) is a participant-centered, health outcome-based approach to a WIC nutrition assessment, which is a required and essential part of the WIC program. It is used to determine eligibility, by identifying nutrition risks, and to personalize WIC nutrition services. • Verification of Certification (VOC) is proof of eligibility for program benefits issued to every participant, including participants in a migrant farmworker family, who are likely to be relocating during the certification period to another state. • Void is the cancellation of food benefits and processed in WIC WISE as not usable. Back to Glossary Navigation W • White is an individual with origins in any of the original peoples of Europe, including, for example, English, German, Irish, Italian, Polish, and Scottish. • WIC Authorized Foods are those supplemental foods authorized by the State for issuance to a particular participant and can be redeemed using the WIC Card. • WIC Authorized Vendor is a sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperative association, corporation, or other business entity operating one or more stores authorized by the State agency to provide authorized supplemental foods to participants under a retail food delivery system. • WIC-eligible nutritional is food specifically formulated to provide calories and nutrients by oral or tube feeding for individuals with a qualifying condition. This may not be a conventional food, drug, flavoring, or enzyme. • WIC Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) administers FMNP benefits in addition to regular WIC benefits to WIC participants. FMNP benefits can be used to purchase eligible locally grown fresh, nutritious, unprepared fruits, vegetables, and fresh-cut herbs, from WIC authorized farmers at WIC-authorized farmers’ markets. • WIC Overseas Program provides WIC services to eligible United States service members (civilian employees, Department of Defense contractors, and members of the uniformed services) and their families on duty outside of the United States. Refer to TRICARE Special Programs for more information about the WIC Overseas Program.

Immunization Screening and Referral WPPM #970-100 JOB AID

Revised February 15, 2026 California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 1

Minimum Immunization Screening and Referral Protocol Local Agency Role How Resources Screening: At a minimum, screen the infant/child’s immunization status by counting the number of doses of DTaP (diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis) vaccine they received in relation to their age. Use the following table to screen immunization status: By 3-mos. of age: At least 1 dose of DTaP By 5-mos. of age: At least 2 doses of DTaP By 7-mos. of age: At least 3 doses of DTaP By 19-mos. of age: At least 4 doses of DTaP The Recommended Immunization Schedule for Persons 0-6 Years provided from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Education: If the infant/child is at risk for being under immunized (i.e. documented record does not list all DTaP vaccinations or a documented immunization record is not provided by the parent/caretaker): WIC staff shall provide information on the recommended immunization schedule appropriate to the current age of the infant/child. No content The MyFamily Immunizations webpage. Referral: If the infant/child is at risk for being under immunized (i.e. documented record does not list all DTaP vaccinations, or a documented immunization record is not provided by the parent/caretaker): WIC staff shall provide referral for immunization services, ideally to the child’s usual source of medical care (or to a no cost/low cost local immunization program). Upon enrollment and at all recertification appointments for children under age two years at risk for being under immunized, WIC staff will provide referral for immunization services, ideally to the child’s usual source of medical care (or to a no cost/low cost local immunization program). LA staff will be expected to develop a local immunization referral list handout for their participants with location, phone number (if any), hours, whether an appointment is necessary, and costs (if any) for immunizations.

body:
JOB AID WPPM #980-1090 Subject: Military Pays Job Aid

Revised California WIC Policy and Procedure Manual Page 1 of 5 March 10, 2026 I. Determining Household Size for Military Families Military personnel serving overseas or on a military base away from home are considered members of the household, even if they do not live in the house. To calculate household size of military families when one or both parents are deployed or stationed abroad, the local agency (LA) staff can: 1. Count the absent parent(s) and the children as one household. This option can only be used if the income of the household can be determined using a Leave and Earnings Statement (LES). 2. Count the children as a separate household. This option can only be used if the household has its own income, such as a children’s allotment. A child’s allotment would be part of a “Discretionary” entry on the LES. The guardian would identify the portion that is allotted for the child. 3. Count the children as part of the economic unit in which they currently live and require proof of income. II. Determining Gross Income for Military Families To determine income for families with household members in the military, staff must review their current LES in addition to other household income sources. III. Determining Combat Pay ** When a household member is deployed to a designated combat zone and receives military combat pay during the deployment, the combat pay must be excluded from the gross income if it meets all three criteria listed below: 1. Received in addition to the service member’s basic pay; 2. Received as a result of the service member’s deployment to, or service in an area that has been designated as a combat zone; and 3. Not received by the service member prior to his/her deployment to, or service in the designated combat zone. A combat zone is any area that the President of the United States designates by Executive Order as an area in which the U.S. Armed Forces are engaging or have engaged in combat. Designated combat zones may be found at the Internal Revenue Service webpage for military combat zones. Information regarding deployment to or service in a combat zone may also be available through military orders or public records on deployment of military units. LA staff may need to request LES documents from prior to the deployment to determine if there has been a difference in income due to the deployment.

Includes personnel directly connected with the administration or enforcement of the program including persons investigating or prosecuting violations in the WIC Program under Federal, State, or local authority.
